input.rationale: Section 5(a) imposes a take-or-pay style monthly minimum on Client for both Hosting Services and Support Services, payable regardless of services actually requested, which breaches our preferred position that fees be for usage or ordered services only. The exposure is aggravated by Section 6, which strips Client of both the right to supporting documentation for, and the right to contest, those minimum monthly fees. While Sections 13 and 14 give Client a non-renewal right and a month-following termination right, that exit does not convert the floor into a true-up and does not cure the unchallengeable nature of the minimum (and the Section 6 cross-references to "Section 4" are themselves erroneous). Because the dollar figures are still blank, deleting the floor is a minimal, low-friction edit that reaches the preferred position; we offer the 12-month, notice-reducible true-up as fallback if TrueLink requires a revenue floor.

proposal.summary: Delete the monthly minimum fee floor so Client pays only for Hosting and Support Services actually requested, and remove the now-moot carve-outs from Client's documentation and dispute rights.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the monthly minimum fee floor in Section 5(a) so that fees are payable only for the Hosting Services and Support Services Client actually requests, consistent with our position against take-or-pay commitments; we also removed the corresponding carve-outs in Section 6 that would otherwise leave Client unable to obtain support for or contest those minimum charges. If TrueLink needs a revenue floor, we can discuss a minimum limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and settled as a true-up rather than a penalty.
